sentences.text: Haolong is known from a nearly complete, articulated skeleton that preserves skin structures.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is catalogued as AGM 16793.
The specimen represents a juvenile measuring about 2.45 meters in length.
Its skin displays a combination of scales and hollow, keratinous spines preserved at the cellular level.
The specific epithet dongi commemorates the Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming.
The genus was described by Huang and colleagues in 2026.
Its fossils were recovered from the Yixian Formation in Liaoning, China.
Additional finds confirm that Haolong material occurs within the Early Cretaceous deposits of China.
Haolong belongs to the iguanodontian ornithopods.
Phylogenetic analysis places it as an early-diverging member of Hadrosauroidea.
The animal lived during the Barremian age of the Early Cretaceous, about 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
Researchers have proposed that the spines could have served for protection, thermoregulation, or tactile sensing.
It remains uncertain whether adult individuals possessed the same spiny integument as the juvenile specimen.
